Title: Authentication is a spoofable header context that fails open to the Stores role
Deficiency_And_Evidence: get_current_user_context reads X-User-Id/X-User-Role/X-User-Department headers; missing headers default to user 'dev_stores_user'/Stores and an unrecognised role string silently falls back to Stores. No token, password or session. Module docstring itself says it must never be deployed (Phase 8 auth not built). Any client can send 'X-User-Role: Admin'.
Dependencies: Choice of identity provider (JWT local / LDAP / SSO) by IT Head; SW-02
Proposed_Remediation: Implement real authentication (token issue/verify, user table, password hashing or directory binding); remove header fallback and default role; fail closed with 401 on missing/invalid identity; refuse to start when ENVIRONMENT=production and SECRET_KEY is the default. Keep a clearly test-only override.
Tests_And_Acceptance: New tests: missing token -> 401; forged X-User-Role header ignored; expired token -> 401; startup refuses default SECRET_KEY in production. Acceptance: no endpoint other than /health and /docs reachable without a valid identity.
Human_Approval_Required: YES - authentication mechanism and user provisioning policy (IT Head / Plant Head)
Blocks_Stage3B_Or_Go_Live: Go-live blocker (Phase 8); not a Stage 3B DB blocker

Title: Stock-moving endpoints have no permission enforcement; actor identity is a client-supplied query parameter defaulting to 'Admin'
Deficiency_And_Evidence: grn.py, issues.py, waste.py, physical_audits.py, ledger.py (POST /entries/{id}/reverse), opening_balances.py, excel_import.py, reconciliation.py GETs and heats GETs do not use require_permission. Actor is taken from Query('Admin') (e.g. grn.py:81,126,137,148; issues.py:83,130; waste.py:83,130; physical_audits.py:81,124; ledger.py:196). Anyone can approve a GRN, reverse a ledger entry or post opening balances as 'Admin'. Permissions RECEIPT_CREATE, ISSUE_CREATE, WASTE_LOG, STOCK_ADJUST, LEDGER_READ, HEAT_LOG_CREATE, HEAT_RECONCILE, AUDIT_READ, USER_MANAGE, ITEM_CREATE, ITEM_UPDATE are defined in ROLE_PERMISSIONS but referenced by zero endpoints (grep of app/api). Heats/aliases/reconciliation use ad-hoc hard-coded role-string tuples instead of the permission matrix.
Dependencies: SW-01 (identity source); decision on which role may approve/reverse each document type (business rule not defined in repo docs)
Proposed_Remediation: Add per-endpoint require_permission dependencies; derive actor ONLY from the authenticated context and delete the actor_id/created_by query params; migrate ad-hoc role tuples to the permission matrix; add approve/reverse permissions (e.g. receipt:approve, ledger:reverse) rather than reusing create permissions.
Tests_And_Acceptance: RBAC matrix test: for every route x role assert 200/403 (parametrised). Test that ?actor_id=... is ignored/removed. Acceptance: every mutating route has a permission dependency; matrix test fails if a new route lacks one.

Title: Costing dashboard sends no identity headers, so every costing call resolves to the default Stores role and is rejected with 403
Deficiency_And_Evidence: CostingDashboard.tsx calls /api/v1/costing/valuation, /heats, /runs, /exceptions, /runs (POST), /runs/compare, /items/{id}/rate-history with plain fetch() and no X-User-Role (lines ~62-200; only a client-side canRunCosting check). Backend costing routes require COSTING_READ/COSTING_CALCULATE, which the Stores role lacks, and the missing-header default is Stores. Backend test_costing_api_permissions passes because it injects headers; no frontend test exists. Found by code inspection; the running UI was not executed in this audit. Same omission in OpeningBalanceView.tsx, LiveInventoryDashboard.tsx, GRN/Issue/Waste/PhysicalAudit views (harmless today only because those endpoints are unauthenticated - see SW-02).
Relevant_Files: frontend/src/components/CostingDashboard.tsx; frontend/src/App.tsx; all components that call fetch()
Dependencies: SW-01/SW-02 (final auth scheme); can be fixed independently for the dev-header scheme
Proposed_Remediation: Introduce one shared apiClient (base URL, auth headers/token, JSON error parsing, 401/403 handling) and replace all raw fetch() calls (72 fetch() call sites across 19 files).
Tests_And_Acceptance: Add Vitest + Testing Library tests with mocked fetch asserting identity headers are sent; manual/e2e check that Management role can open Costing tabs against a running backend. Acceptance: no raw fetch() outside apiClient (lint rule).
Blocks_Stage3B_Or_Go_Live: Software defect; prevents Phase 6 UI use today

Title: Ledger immutability is by convention only; entry numbering and negative-stock check are race-prone
Deficiency_And_Evidence: No DB trigger/REVOKE preventing UPDATE/DELETE on stock_ledger_entries (grep of models/migrations: only a UniqueConstraint). generate_ledger_entry_number uses COUNT(*)+1 (ledger_service.py:24-33); two concurrent postings can compute the same number and one fails on the UNIQUE entry_number. Issue approval reads balance then inserts with no row lock or serialisable transaction (ledger_service.py:150), so concurrent issues can overdraw. Reversals of inward entries also check-then-write. Also posting_group_id/reconciliation run_number use second-resolution timestamps. SQLite tests cannot expose any of this.
Dependencies: PostgreSQL non-prod instance (INF-01, gates G12) to verify
Proposed_Remediation: New Alembic revision adding BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE triggers raising on stock_ledger_entries; replace COUNT numbering with a PostgreSQL sequence (or advisory lock); lock per-item (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on item row or pg_advisory_xact_lock) around balance check + insert.
Tests_And_Acceptance: PostgreSQL-only tests: UPDATE/DELETE on ledger raises; 20 concurrent threaded issues against stock of N never drive balance below zero; concurrent postings produce unique gap-free-or-unique numbers. Acceptance: tests green on PG 16 on port 5439.
Human_Approval_Required: No for code; YES to run migration (Lead DBA, after G1)

Title: Opening valuation endpoint mutates an existing approved rate in place with no history or audit trail
Deficiency_And_Evidence: propose_opening_valuation overwrites opening_rate_ex_gst, baseline_date, notes, approved_by/at on the existing row and re-marks APPROVED (costing.py:726-737). Previous rate is lost, yet it drives weighted-average costing and every historical costing run's reproducibility. No audit-log table exists for item_opening_valuations (migration 005).
Dependencies: SW-04; Gate G3 supplies the real rates (BIZ-01)
Proposed_Remediation: Make valuations versioned/append-only (superseded_by, created_by, approved_by), add an audit table, forbid edits after a costing run has consumed the valuation.
Tests_And_Acceptance: Tests: second submission creates a new version and keeps the first; costing run snapshots remain reproducible after a revaluation. Acceptance: no UPDATE of opening_rate_ex_gst anywhere.
Human_Approval_Required: YES - who may approve opening rates (Finance Head)
Blocks_Stage3B_Or_Go_Live: Needed before opening rates are loaded

Title: No controlled path to cancel/reverse an approved GRN, issue slip or waste disposition
Deficiency_And_Evidence: cancel_grn and cancel_material_issue reject APPROVED documents with 'Requires reversal authorization' (grn_service.py:208-211; issue_service.py:180-183) but no such workflow exists. The only correction tool is raw ledger-entry reversal (ledger_service.py:321), which does not change the source document status, does not reverse all lines of a document together, and has no UI (no frontend call to /reverse; grep of frontend/src). Costing handles REVERSAL movements (costing_service.py:225) but there is no test of a reversal flowing through a costing run.
Dependencies: SW-02; business rule on who authorises reversals and time limits (undefined)
Proposed_Remediation: Add document-level reversal workflow (REVERSAL_PENDING -> REVERSED) that posts compensating entries for all lines atomically, updates source status and audit log, and exposes a UI action with mandatory reason.
Tests_And_Acceptance: Tests: approve GRN -> reverse -> balance restored, status REVERSED, double reversal blocked; reversal of issue after later receipts; costing run before/after reversal. Acceptance: ledger sum equals expected and costing exceptions list stays consistent.

Title: Physical-audit variance is frozen at draft time and posted unchanged on approval
Deficiency_And_Evidence: create_physical_audit computes system_quantity via get_material_stock_balance(as_of=audit_date) once (physical_audit_service.py:~76-84). Approval posts line.variance as stored (ledger_service.py:264-318). Any ledger entry dated <= audit_date posted between draft and approval (or a reversal) makes the adjustment wrong, and nothing re-validates. The only test (test_physical_audit_variance_and_adjustment_posting) covers the happy path.
Dependencies: None for the check; stocktake evidence (BIZ-05) for real data
Proposed_Remediation: Recompute system quantity at approval and reject (or require re-submission) when it differs from the stored snapshot; store both values on the posting.
Tests_And_Acceptance: Test: create audit, post a back-dated receipt, approve -> blocked with clear message. Acceptance: posted adjustment always brings the ledger to the counted quantity.

Title: Reconciliation run numbers can collide on the same day
Deficiency_And_Evidence: run_number = REC-YYYYMMDD-{int(timestamp % 10000):04d} (reconciliation_service.py:131); the value repeats every 10,000 seconds (~2.8 h) so two runs on one date can produce the same number and violate UNIQUE(run_number) (migration 004). Costing run number uses a separate generator (costing_service.py:77).
Proposed_Remediation: Use a DB sequence or max(existing)+1 inside the transaction.
Tests_And_Acceptance: Test creating runs with a frozen clock 10,000 s apart. Acceptance: no IntegrityError, numbers unique.

Title: Test and runtime bootstrap depend on the PostgreSQL driver even for SQLite tests; dependencies unpinned
Deficiency_And_Evidence: tests/conftest.py imports app.main -> app/db/session.py builds a psycopg engine with connect_args={'connect_timeout':3} at import time. In this audit environment pytest failed at collection with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'psycopg' until the driver was supplied. requirements.txt uses '>=' for every package with no lock file; runtime here is Python 3.14.6; Starlette/FastAPI deprecation warnings (HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY, httpx TestClient) already appear.
Proposed_Remediation: Pin versions (constraints/lock file), declare supported Python version, create engine lazily, and make driver args dialect-aware; replace deprecated constants.
Tests_And_Acceptance: Acceptance: fresh venv from lock file runs pytest green with zero warnings from our code; documented in SETUP_GUIDE.
